concept_source: Operator HelicopterBench concept, established 2026-10-29; ten gameplay requirements preserved verbatim; one testability requirement (window.__HELICOPTER_STATE__ state contract) added at freezing so every required mechanic is mechanically verifiable without source inspection. Methodology helicopterbench/3 (owner-approved prospective 2026-11-11) changes ONLY the scoring methodology relative to the frozen v1.0.0 fixture: the task, extraction contract, budget numbers, sandbox isolation and the state contract are byte-identical. The frozen v1.0.0 fixture and the original /1 and /2 evidence and reconstruction are unaffected.
one_shot_rules: One frozen prompt; one generation opportunity; the first completed submission is the submission; no model feedback or corrective conversation; no agent repair of submitted code; no retries; no best-of selection. Incomplete generations take the accepted budget disposition, never a completed-incorrect-game classification.

task.user_task:
Build a complete, immediately playable helicopter-style game as ONE standalone HTML file. Reply with exactly one fenced code block tagged html containing the entire file (HTML, CSS and JavaScript included; no other text).

Required gameplay:
1. A scrolling green cave or corridor the player flies through.
2. A helicopter the player controls with the mouse.
3. Holding the mouse button makes the helicopter ascend; gravity pulls it down when the button is released.
4. Moving hazards or obstacles inside the corridor.
5. Working collision detection (walls, obstacles, and floor/ceiling all end the run).
6. Difficulty that increases as the run continues.
7. A distance-based score that updates during play.
8. A clearly visible game-over state when a run ends.
9. A working restart: after game over, clicking the mouse starts a fresh run.
10. Immediate playability when the file is opened in a modern browser.

No external libraries, frameworks, hosted scripts, downloaded assets, or network access of any kind: everything must be inside the one submitted file and must work offline.

Required testability contract (used for mechanical gameplay verification): while running, the page must keep a global object window.__HELICOPTER_STATE__ updated with numeric fields y (helicopter vertical position), score, difficulty, distance, a numeric field speed (current corridor scroll speed), boolean fields crashed and gameOver, and an array obstacles whose entries expose x (and may expose top/bottom). State must refresh every frame. Clicking after game over must start a fresh run within the same page.

budget_proposal.rationale: One-shot single-file game: the calibration reference implementation is 3940 bytes (~1300 completion tokens incl. reasoning overhead); 8192 completion tokens give >5x headroom for any reasonable implementation without adopting Advanced Coding's 12288. 300 s accommodates the longest plausible single generation at reference throughput. Values are byte-identical to the operator-ACCEPTED 2026-11-07 budget (deployment.method_acceptance); no new budget machinery is introduced by methodology /3.
budget_proposal.extraction: Deterministic: if the completed reply contains a fenced code block tagged html, the FIRST such block is the artifact; else if the trimmed reply starts with '<' and contains '</html>', the whole reply is the artifact; otherwise there is no extractable artifact (completed-but-artifact-deficient FAIL). The extracted bytes are never altered.

scoring.automated_rubric: True native 100-point mechanical rubric (methodology helicopterbench/3, owner-approved prospective 2026-11-11): the same 14 behavioral subchecks with category weights launch_and_rendering 20 (no_runtime_exceptions 8, canvas_present 6, animation_liveliness 6), controls_and_physics 20 (input_causes_ascent 7, gravity_causes_descent 7, controls_state_numeric 6), obstacles_and_collision 20 (obstacles_present 7, obstacles_advance 6, collision_produces_game_over 7), score_failure_restart 20 (score_accrues 10, game_over_visible_text 5, restart_resets 5), course_and_difficulty 20 (difficulty_increases 10, speed_increases 10). The single final score IS the exact earned mechanical total out of 100 - there is no normalization of a 90-point raw total and no per-category rounding. The extraction contract, the browser-verification isolation and the window.__HELICOPTER_STATE__ contract are byte-identical to methodologies /1 and /2, so preserved verification records remain reconstruction-compatible.
scoring.human_playtesting: Independent, attributed human playtesting is a separate acceptance channel and is never merged into the automated score. The reviewer plays the exact submitted game (bytes unchanged, bound by SHA-256 to the finalized automated evidence) inside a safe self-contained local review surface, and answers the 14-item checklist: Yes earns the full item points, No earns zero, an unanswered item leaves the review UNRESOLVED. Running earned points are never a final score until every item is answered and every dispute is reconciled. Every material disagreement with the automated record is resolved only by an explicit reconciliation record carrying evidence, rationale and the attributed reviewer; automated results are never averaged or overwritten. The operating agent never invents human answers and never produces a model self-score. Recorded mechanical evidence (numeric state samples) may supplement the reviewer's judgment for numeric-state items.

verification.isolation: Submitted games are untrusted: each runs once inside a disposable bubblewrap namespace (host root never mounted; isolated user/pid/ipc/uts/network namespaces; loopback-only; cleared environment; fresh tmpfs profile; hard host-side timeout). A self-contained CDP driver inside the namespace launches the deployed browser binary headlessly, drives REAL input events, samples the frozen state contract and frames, and writes one bounded JSON record. No artifact code executes on the host. This existing automated sandbox is the independent mechanical verifier for methodology /3 and is unchanged.
verification.browser_discovery: An existing installed Chromium-family binary is used (discovery list in welp_next.browser_harness; this host: brave-browser-stable). No browser is downloaded or installed by WELP; if none exists the section reports a technical environment failure, never a model outcome.
verification.human_review_boundary: The human playtesting surface is a small self-contained local HTML checklist, opened by the attributed reviewer in their own browser. It embeds the exact SHA-256-bound game bytes, refuses to mount them unless the recomputed digest matches the finalized binding, and runs the game only inside an opaque-origin sandboxed iframe (sandbox="allow-scripts" with strict content-security and navigation denial; no same-origin, no host filesystem, no CDP, no display-socket or network access). The independent mechanical verifier remains the existing bubblewrap CDP sandbox; the iframe route is the human play channel only, and its limitations are stated in the review surface itself. The automated record is never altered by human review.
